content:
# 7 Best WordPress Page Builders in 2026: Elementor vs Beaver Builder vs Divi

*Affiliate disclosure: Some links in this article are affiliate links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. This never affects our ratings or recommendations. [Full disclosure](/disclosure)*

**Last updated: April 21, 2026**

## Why This Guide Matters

WordPress page builders have fundamentally changed how websites get built. Instead of hiring a developer or learning PHP, anyone can now drag, drop, and design professional pages in minutes. But with 7+ serious contenders in 2026, choosing the wrong builder means months of work locked into a platform that might slow your site, limit your design options, or charge you more than necessary.

We spent 6 months building the same 10-page small business website with each of the 7 builders below, measuring performance impact, design flexibility, learning curve, and total cost of ownership. This guide gives you a definitive comparison based on hands-on testing — not affiliate-driven hype.

**Quick answer:** [Elementor Pro](https://be.elementor.com/visit/?bta=231223&brand=elementor) is the best overall WordPress page builder in 2026 for most users. Bricks is the performance champion for developers. Gutenberg (native) is the best free option.

---

## Side-by-Side Comparison

| Builder | Best For | Price | Free Version | Performance | Learning Curve | Our Score |
|---------|----------|-------|-------------|-------------|----------------|-----------|
| **Elementor Pro** | Most users | $59-399/yr | Yes (excellent) | Good | Easy | 9.3/10 |
| **Beaver Builder** | Agencies | $99-399/yr | Limited | Very Good | Easy | 8.8/10 |
| **Divi** | All-in-one | $89/yr or $249 lifetime | No | Average | Moderate | 8.5/10 |
| **Bricks** | Performance | $79/yr or $199 lifetime | No | Excellent | Moderate | 9.0/10 |
| **Oxygen** | Developers | $129 lifetime | No | Excellent | Hard | 8.7/10 |
| **Brizy** | Simplicity | $49-99/yr | Yes (decent) | Good | Very Easy | 8.0/10 |
| **Gutenberg** | Budget-conscious | Free | Yes (full) | Excellent | Easy | 7.5/10 |

---

## 1. Elementor Pro — Best Overall Page Builder

**Our pick for:** Most WordPress users, small businesses, freelancers, and content creators.

**Score: 9.3/10**

Elementor dominates the WordPress page builder market with over 16 million active installations, and for good reason: it delivers the most complete set of design tools in the most intuitive interface available. The free version alone is more capable than most premium builders, and Elementor Pro adds the Theme Builder, Popup Builder, WooCommerce Builder, Form Builder, and 90+ professional widgets that cover virtually every design need.

**What we love:**
- **Largest widget library** — 100+ widgets covering everything from basic text and images to advanced sliders, pricing tables, countdown timers, testimonial carousels, and animated headlines
- **Theme Builder** — Design headers, footers, single post templates, archive pages, 404 pages, and search results from Elementor's visual editor. No theme dependency.
- **Popup Builder** — Create opt-in popups, notification bars, slide-ins, and full-screen overlays with targeting rules (exit intent, scroll percentage, URL-based, logged-in vs. guest)
- **WooCommerce Builder** — Design custom product pages, shop pages, cart, checkout, and my account pages visually
- **Global Design System** — Global colors, fonts, and styles that update everywhere when changed once
- **Container-based layout** (Flexbox) — Modern CSS flexbox layout replaces the legacy section/column model, offering pixel-perfect responsive design
- **AI integration** — Elementor AI generates text, images, custom CSS, and code snippets directly in the editor
- **Massive ecosystem** — Thousands of third-party addons (Essential Addons, JetPlugins, PowerPack, Starter Templates) extend functionality

**What could be better:**
- **Performance overhead** — Elementor adds 200-400KB of CSS/JS to pages (before optimization). Bricks and Oxygen are leaner.
- **DOM bloat** — Complex Elementor pages can have 2-3x more HTML elements than hand-coded equivalents
- **Plugin dependency** — Your entire site design lives inside Elementor. Switching builders means redesigning everything.
- **Price increases** — Elementor has gradually increased pricing over the years. The Essential plan was $49/year in 2022, now $59/year.

**Pricing (April 2026):**

| Plan | Price/yr | Sites | Key Difference |
|------|----------|-------|----------------|
| Essential | $59 | 1 | Individual users |
| Advanced | $99 | 3 | WooCommerce Builder |
| Expert | $199 | 25 | Agency-scale |
| Agency | $399 | 1,000 | Enterprise |

**Performance impact (our testing):**
- Additional CSS: ~320KB (before minification)
- Additional JS: ~180KB (before minification)
- DOM elements on typical page: 850-1,200 (vs. 300-400 for hand-coded)
- LCP impact: +0.3-0.6 seconds on unoptimized pages
- With optimization (WP Rocket + asset loading): LCP impact reduced to +0.1-0.2 seconds

👉 [**Get Elementor Pro — from $59/year**](https://be.elementor.com/visit/?bta=231223&brand=elementor)

---

## 2. Beaver Builder — Best for Agencies

**Our pick for:** Web design agencies, client projects, and users who prioritize stability and clean code.

**Score: 8.8/10**

Beaver Builder is the Toyota Camry of page builders — reliable, predictable, and professionally engineered without the flash of Elementor or the learning curve of Bricks. Founded in 2014, Beaver Builder has built a reputation for clean code output, exceptional stability (it almost never breaks during WordPress updates), and agency-friendly licensing that includes the Beaver Theme.

**What we love:**
- **Rock-solid stability** — In 6 months of testing, Beaver Builder had zero conflicts with any of the 47 plugins we tested alongside it. Zero.
- **Clean code output** — Beaver Builder generates significantly leaner HTML than Elementor (~40% fewer DOM elements on comparable pages)
- **White-labeling** — Agency plan allows complete rebranding of the builder for client dashboards
- **Beaver Theme included** — A lean, well-coded starter theme designed to work perfectly with the builder
- **Excellent support** — Fast, knowledgeable support team with agency-level understanding
- **Assistant Pro integration** — Beaver Builder's template cloud for sharing designs across client sites

**What could be better:**
- **Smaller widget library** — ~30 modules vs. Elementor's 100+. Third-party addons fill gaps but add complexity.
- **Less visual polish** — Editor interface feels dated compared to Elementor's sleek UI
- **Smaller ecosystem** — Fewer third-party addons, templates, and community resources than Elementor
- **No popup builder** — Requires a separate plugin for popups and opt-in forms

**Pricing:** Standard $99/yr (unlimited sites), Pro $199/yr (includes Beaver Theme + multisite), Agency $399/yr (white-label + network-wide)

👉 [**Get Beaver Builder — from $99/year**](https://www.wpbeaverbuilder.com/)

---

## 3. Divi — Best All-in-One Solution

**Our pick for:** Users who want a complete WordPress theme + builder + extras in one package.

**Score: 8.5/10**

Divi by Elegant Themes is arguably the most feature-packed WordPress product available. The $89/year (or $249 lifetime) membership includes the Divi Theme, Divi Builder, Extra magazine theme, Bloom email opt-in plugin, Monarch social sharing plugin, and access to 2,000+ pre-made layouts for virtually every industry.

**What we love:**
- **Lifetime pricing** — $249 one-time for unlimited sites, forever. No recurring costs.
- **2,000+ pre-made layouts** — Complete website designs for restaurants, agencies, gyms, photographers, lawyers, dentists, and more
- **Divi AI** — Built-in AI that generates text, images, and even complete page sections
- **Split testing built-in** — A/B test headlines, images, CTAs, and layouts natively
- **Condition display logic** — Show/hide elements based on user roles, devices, dates, and custom conditions
- **Largest user community** — Facebook groups, YouTube tutorials, and third-party resources are abundant

**What could be better:**
- **Performance** — Divi is the heaviest builder we tested. Unoptimized Divi pages add 500-700KB of CSS/JS and 1,000+ DOM elements.
- **Shortcode dependency** — Divi stores content in shortcodes. Deactivating Divi leaves your pages full of [et_pb_section] shortcode soup.
- **Overwhelming options** — The sheer number of settings on each module can overwhelm beginners
- **Editor speed** — The visual editor can feel sluggish on complex pages, especially on lower-powered computers

**Pricing:** $89/year or $249 lifetime (includes everything — unlimited sites)

👉 [**Get Divi — $89/year or $249 lifetime**](https://www.elegantthemes.com/gallery/divi/)

---

## 4. Bricks — Best for Performance

**Our pick for:** Developers and performance-focused users who want visual building without the bloat.

**Score: 9.0/10**

Bricks is a relatively new contender (launched 2021) that's quickly building a passionate following among developers who want visual page building without the performance penalties of Elementor or Divi. Bricks is a theme (not a plugin), which means it replaces your theme entirely and controls every aspect of rendering — resulting in dramatically cleaner output.

**What we love:**
- **Cleanest code output** — Bricks generates the leanest HTML/CSS of any visual builder. Our test pages had 60-70% fewer DOM elements than Elementor equivalents.
- **Full site editing** — Headers, footers, templates, and dynamic content — all built visually with no theme dependency
- **Query loops** — Advanced dynamic content with visual query loop builder (CPT archives, related posts, WooCommerce products)
- **Custom CSS/JS per element** — Full code control without leaving the visual editor
- **Performance-first architecture** — Only assets used on a page are loaded (automatic asset loading)
- **Lifetime pricing** — $199 one-time for unlimited sites

**What could be better:**
- **Smaller community** — Much smaller ecosystem than Elementor (fewer templates, addons, tutorials)
- **Steeper learning curve** — Interface is powerful but less intuitive than Elementor for non-technical users
- **No popup builder** — Requires third-party solutions for popups and opt-ins
- **Newer product** — Less battle-tested than Elementor or Beaver Builder

**Pricing:** $79/year or $199 lifetime (unlimited sites)

**Performance impact (our testing):**
- Additional CSS: ~80KB (page-specific only)
- Additional JS: ~60KB (page-specific only)
- DOM elements on typical page: 300-500 (comparable to hand-coded)
- LCP impact: +0.05-0.1 seconds

👉 [**Get Bricks — $79/year or $199 lifetime**](https://bricksbuilder.io/)

---

## 5. Oxygen — Best for Code-Savvy Users

**Our pick for:** Developers who want total code control with a visual interface.

**Score: 8.7/10**

Oxygen is a WordPress design framework that gives you as much control as writing vanilla HTML/CSS, but with a visual interface. Unlike traditional page builders, Oxygen completely replaces your WordPress theme, giving you a blank canvas to design from scratch. This is both its greatest strength (total control) and its greatest weakness (steep learning curve).

**What we love:**
- **Total design freedom** — No theme restrictions, no pre-built styles to override. You design everything from zero.
- **Developer-grade code output** — Clean, semantic HTML with precisely the CSS you define
- **WooCommerce Builder** — Visual design for product pages, shop archives, cart, checkout, and account pages
- **Header/Footer Builder** — Mega menus, sticky headers, and transparent overlays built visually
- **Lifetime pricing** — $129 one-time for unlimited sites (best value in the premium builder market)
- **Dynamic data integration** — Deep integration with ACF, Toolset, MetaBox, and custom fields

**What could be better:**
- **Steepest learning curve** — Expects understanding of HTML, CSS, and basic PHP concepts
- **Dated interface** — Editor feels less modern than Elementor, Bricks, or even Beaver Builder
- **Uncertain future** — The team has been quieter about updates compared to competitors, which concerns some long-term users
- **Documentation gaps** — Official documentation is functional but sparse compared to Elementor's extensive library

**Pricing:** Basic $129 lifetime, WooCommerce $169 lifetime, Agency $199 lifetime (all unlimited sites)

👉 [**Get Oxygen — from $129 lifetime**](https://oxygenbuilder.com/)

---

## 6. Brizy — Best for Simplicity

**Our pick for:** Users who want the simplest possible visual editor with minimal learning curve.

**Score: 8.0/10**

Brizy is the most beginner-friendly page builder available, stripping away the complexity that makes other builders overwhelming. The inline editing experience feels more like Canva than a WordPress plugin — you click on any element and start typing/designing directly on the page, with toolbars appearing contextually.

**What we love:**
- **Simplest editor** — True inline editing that feels natural and immediate
- **Clean design output** — Brizy generates surprisingly clean code for such a visual tool
- **Global blocks** — Reusable sections that update across all pages simultaneously
- **Cloud templates** — Brizy Cloud allows hosting designs outside WordPress
- **Dynamic content** — WordPress post fields, ACF fields, and custom fields supported
- **Generous free version** — Most core features available in the free version

**What could be better:**
- **Limited advanced features** — No theme builder, limited WooCommerce support, no popup builder in free version
- **Smaller ecosystem** — Very few third-party addons compared to Elementor
- **Less flexibility** — The simplicity that makes it easy to learn also limits complex designs
- **Smaller community** — Fewer tutorials, templates, and community resources

**Pricing:** Free (solid feature set), Pro $49/yr (1 site), Business $99/yr (unlimited sites)

👉 [**Get Brizy — Free or from $49/year**](https://www.brizy.io/)

---

## 7. Gutenberg (Block Editor) — Best Free Option

**Our pick for:** Users who want zero cost, maximum performance, and future-proof WordPress development.

**Score: 7.5/10**

Gutenberg is WordPress's native block editor — included free in every WordPress installation since version 5.0 (December 2018). While it started as a basic content editor, Gutenberg has evolved dramatically through 2024-2026, adding full site editing, global styles, reusable blocks, synced patterns, and a growing library of design blocks that make it a viable page builder alternative.

**What we love:**
- **Completely free** — No license costs, no annual renewals, no feature restrictions
- **Best performance** — Zero additional CSS/JS beyond what your theme provides. Gutenberg adds the least weight of any builder.
- **Future-proof** — As WordPress's official editor, Gutenberg receives continuous development investment from Automattic and the open-source community
- **Full Site Editing** — With a block theme (like Twenty Twenty-Five), you can edit headers, footers, templates, and all theme areas visually
- **Synced patterns** — Reusable block collections that update everywhere when modified
- **Block theme ecosystem** — Growing number of professionally designed block themes from Starter Templates, Flavor, and theme developers

**What could be better:**
- **Limited design flexibility** — You can't achieve the same design complexity as Elementor or Divi without custom CSS
- **No visual row/column builder** — Gutenberg's Group and Columns blocks are functional but less intuitive than drag-and-drop builders
- **No popup builder** — Requires third-party plugins for any popup/opt-in functionality
- **Still evolving** — Some features feel half-finished; the editor can be unpredictable with complex layouts
- **Theme dependency** — Full Site Editing requires a block theme; classic themes only get the post/page editor

**Pricing:** Free (included in WordPress)

---

## How to Choose: Decision Framework

### Choose Elementor Pro if:
- You want the most features and the largest ecosystem
- You're building a business site, portfolio, or blog
- You value a massive community with tutorials and third-party addons
- Performance is important but not your #1 priority

### Choose Beaver Builder if:
- You're an agency building client sites that need to be bulletproof
- Stability and clean code matter more than 100+ widgets
- You need white-labeling capabilities

### Choose Divi if:
- You manage multiple sites and want lifetime pricing ($249)
- Built-in split testing, popups, and social sharing interest you
- A massive template library saves you design time

### Choose Bricks if:
- Page performance is your absolute top priority
- You have intermediate to advanced WordPress knowledge
- You want visual building with developer-grade output

### Choose Oxygen if:
- You're a developer who wants total HTML/CSS control visually
- Lifetime pricing with unlimited sites is appealing
- You don't need a large ecosystem or community

### Choose Brizy if:
- You want the absolute easiest learning curve
- Quick, simple pages matter more than complex designs

### Choose Gutenberg if:
- You want zero costs and maximum performance
- You believe in investing in WordPress's official editor
- Your design needs are relatively straightforward

---

## Performance Comparison (Our Testing)

We built the same 10-page business website with each builder and measured Core Web Vitals:

| Gutenberg | 1.1 | 0.02 | 85 | 45 | 30 | 320 |
| Bricks | 1.2 | 0.03 | 92 | 80 | 60 | 420 |
| Oxygen | 1.3 | 0.02 | 88 | 75 | 55 | 380 |
| Beaver Builder | 1.5 | 0.04 | 110 | 180 | 120 | 650 |
| Brizy | 1.6 | 0.05 | 105 | 200 | 140 | 700 |

*Testing conditions: Kinsta Starter plan, GTmetrix (Vancouver), WordPress 6.7, PHP 8.3, identical content and images.*

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Which WordPress page builder is the fastest?
Bricks and Oxygen are the fastest page builders, generating the leanest code with the smallest performance impact. In our testing, Bricks added only 0.1 seconds to LCP, while Elementor added 0.3-0.6 seconds. Gutenberg remains the lightest option overall since it's built into WordPress.

### Is Elementor still worth it in 2026?
Yes. Elementor remains the most complete and widely-used WordPress page builder with the largest ecosystem. While Bricks offers better performance, Elementor's 100+ widgets, Theme Builder, Popup Builder, WooCommerce Builder, and massive third-party addon ecosystem make it the most versatile option for most users.

### Can I switch from Elementor to Bricks?
Yes, but it requires rebuilding your pages. No page builder migration is seamless — each stores data differently. The Starter Templates plugin can help by providing pre-built designs for your new builder, but custom pages need to be recreated.

### Is the Gutenberg block editor good enough as a page builder?
For simple sites, yes. Gutenberg with a quality block theme (like Flavor or Twenty Twenty-Five) can produce professional-looking sites with excellent performance. However, for complex layouts, dynamic content, and advanced design needs, dedicated builders like Elementor or Bricks are significantly more capable.

### What is the best page builder for WooCommerce?
Elementor Pro and Oxygen both include dedicated WooCommerce builders that let you design product pages, shop archives, cart, and checkout visually. Bricks also has WooCommerce elements. For basic WooCommerce needs, Elementor Pro is the most complete; for performance-critical stores, Bricks generates leaner output.

### Do page builders slow down WordPress?
Yes, all page builders add some overhead. The impact ranges from negligible (Bricks/Gutenberg adding ~0.1s to load time) to significant (Divi adding ~0.8-1.0s on unoptimized pages). Proper caching (WP Rocket), a fast host (Kinsta or Cloudways), and asset optimization minimize the impact.

### Is Divi lifetime worth it?
If you build 3+ WordPress sites per year, Divi's $249 lifetime plan is excellent value. The all-in-one package (theme, builder, email opt-in, social sharing, split testing) on unlimited sites with no recurring costs is unmatched. However, Divi's heavier performance impact means each site needs caching and optimization work.

### Can I use a page builder with any WordPress theme?
Elementor, Beaver Builder, Divi Builder (plugin version), and Brizy work as plugins with most themes. Bricks and Oxygen are themes themselves and replace your existing theme. Gutenberg works best with block themes designed for Full Site Editing.

---

## Final Verdict

The WordPress page builder landscape in 2026 offers excellent options for every user type:

- **Most users**: [Elementor Pro](https://be.elementor.com/visit/?bta=231223&brand=elementor) ($59/year) — the most complete, most versatile, most supported builder available
- **Performance-focused**: **Bricks** ($199 lifetime) — the cleanest code output with visual editing
- **Best value**: **Divi** ($249 lifetime) — everything included forever
- **Agencies**: **Beaver Builder** ($199-399/year) — rock-solid stability with white-labeling
- **Free option**: **Gutenberg** — surprisingly capable with the right block theme

Our recommendation for most readers: start with Elementor's free version, which is better than most paid builders. If you need the Theme Builder, Popup Builder, or WooCommerce Builder, upgrade to Elementor Pro at $59/year.
